answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by requiring each identity to lock a refundable stake that is slashed on proven fraud, with reputation growing only through verified, attested work. Like a sparrow guarding a grove, every agent earns trust slowly: each completed job adds a small signed record, so a fresh identity holds no nectar of credibility. An attacker who spawns a thousand fake agents must fund a thousand stakes and pay for a thousand histories of real work, while honest agents keep their stake and earned reputation. Forging identities costs more than the fraud they could commit.
